---
id: brute-force-password-spray
title: Brute force and password spray
summary: Many failed sign-ins against one or more accounts, from one or many sources. The question that matters is whether any attempt succeeded.
use_when: A detection reports repeated failed authentication against our accounts or services.
prerequisites: Authentication logs from the targeted systems with the outcome of each attempt.
version: 1
priority: 50
review_every_days: 180
mitre: [T1110]
applies_when:
  rule_ids: [mail_auth, waf_auth, web_auth, roundcube_login, postfix, sshd, linux_auth, winlogon]
  entity_types: [ip, user, host]
retrieval_queries:
  - brute force lockout policy runbook
  - MITRE T1110 password spray
  - credential stuffing detection thresholds
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/
  - https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final
---

## Triage

### Is the source internal or external? {#source-scope kind=check evidence=note}
Focus: the source IP, its network zone and the asset inventory.
Escalate if: an internal host that is not an approved scanner, or an external address with a hostile reputation.
Benign if: an approved vulnerability scanner or a known test.

### How many accounts were tried? {#accounts-tried kind=lookup}
Focus: many accounts from one source is a spray; one account is targeted guessing.

```lookup
tool: log_stats
filter:
  ip: "{{entity.ip}}"
group_by: [user]
window: case_first_seen-1h..case_last_seen+1h
limit: 20
run: on_attach
```

### Reputation of the source IP {#source-reputation kind=lookup}
Focus: known hostile, anonymising or unexpected geography for this account.

```lookup
tool: enrich
indicator: "{{entity.ip}}"
window: case_first_seen-1h..case_last_seen+1h
limit: 20
run: on_attach
```

## Investigate

### Did any attempt succeed after the failures? {#success-after-failures kind=lookup}
Focus: a success for the same source or account during or right after the failures is the decisive signal.

```lookup
tool: log_stats
filter:
  ip: "{{entity.ip}}"
group_by: [event.outcome, user]
window: case_first_seen-1h..case_last_seen+1h
limit: 20
run: on_attach
```

If the source changed address, repeat the check for each targeted account.

The outcome comes from the ECS field `event.outcome`. A source that names it differently shows the attempts without their outcome, so check the outcome in the logs before you conclude that nothing succeeded.

### Are the targeted accounts privileged or service accounts? {#privileged-accounts kind=check evidence=note}
Escalate if: an administrator, service or shared account was targeted, or any attempt succeeded.
Benign if: a few failures followed by a normal sign-in from the user's usual device and place.

### Other cases from this source in 30 days {#related-cases kind=lookup}
Focus: repeat activity from the same source, and the accounts it went after before.

```lookup
tool: related_cases
filter:
  entity: "{{entity.ip}}"
window: case_last_seen-30d..case_last_seen
limit: 10
run: on_attach
```

### Is this a confirmed compromise? {#decide kind=decision}
Escalate if: any attempt succeeded and the session then did something unusual, or a hostile source is still active.
Benign if: no attempt succeeded and the failures match a user error or an approved test.
Options:
- confirmed: Confirmed compromise
- suspicious: Suspicious, not confirmed
- benign: Benign | skips: block-source, reset-accounts

Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.

## Contain

### Block the source at the edge {#block-source kind=action optional react=RA3101}

Block the source at the firewall or WAF. Record where you blocked it and the change reference.

### Reset or lock the affected accounts {#reset-accounts kind=action d3fend=D3-AL}

Reset the password and end the sessions of every account that signed in from the source; lock any that you cannot reset now.

## Close and learn

### Tell the account owners {#tell-owners kind=record}

Tell each account owner what happened and what changed for them.

### Record the outcome and what you would change {#record-outcome kind=record}

Write what happened and whether lockout, MFA or detection thresholds should change.

definition.title: Cloud identity and access key compromise
definition.summary: A cloud identity, role, token or access key is used in a way its owner did not intend. Scope what it can reach, then rotate it.
definition.use_when: A detection reports anomalous role assumptions, OAuth token replay, unusual access key use or risky service principal sign-ins.
definition.prerequisites: Cloud audit logs (for example CloudTrail or Entra ID sign-in and audit logs); access to disable keys and revoke sessions.

steps.title: Which identity or key is involved and what can it reach?
steps.focus: the user, role, service principal or access key, and the permissions attached to it.
steps.escalate_if: the identity can change permissions, read sensitive data or create credentials.
steps.benign_if: a low-privilege test identity with no access to production.

steps.title: Recent API activity by this identity
steps.instructions: Actions come from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record that field, no actions are listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing happened.
steps.focus: which actions it called, how often, and whether any failed.

steps.title: Calls from new locations or unusual services
steps.instructions: Actions come from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record that field, no actions are listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing happened.
steps.focus: source addresses, regions and services the identity has not used before.

steps.title: Were new keys, roles or policies created?
steps.escalate_if: new access keys, roles, policies, consents or federation settings appeared.
steps.benign_if: a recorded change by an approved automation or administrator.

steps.title: Compromised, suspicious or benign?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: an unexpected session changed privileges or credentials, granted consent, or reached sensitive resources.
steps.benign_if: an unusual location or reputation alone, with no change and an expected owner.

steps.title: Disable or rotate the key and revoke sessions
steps.instructions: Disable or rotate the key, revoke the identity's sessions and tokens, and record the change reference.

steps.title: Remove attacker-created keys, roles and resources
steps.instructions: Remove every key, role, policy, consent and resource the attacker created, after you have recorded them.

steps.title: Are workloads using the new credentials?
steps.escalate_if: the old key is still in use, or new unexpected activity appears.
steps.benign_if: every workload runs on the new credentials and the old ones are gone.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write how the identity was exposed and what would have limited it, such as shorter-lived keys or tighter permissions.

## Triage

### Which identity or key is involved and what can it reach? {#identity-scope kind=check evidence=note}
Focus: the user, role, service principal or access key, and the permissions attached to it.
Escalate if: the identity can change permissions, read sensitive data or create credentials.
Benign if: a low-privilege test identity with no access to production.

### Recent API activity by this identity {#api-activity kind=lookup}
Focus: which actions it called, how often, and whether any failed.

```lookup
tool: log_stats
filter:
  user: "{{entity.user}}"
group_by: [action]
window: case_last_seen-1d..case_last_seen+1h
limit: 20
run: on_attach
```

Actions come from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record that field, no actions are listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing happened.

## Investigate

### Calls from new locations or unusual services {#new-locations kind=lookup}
Focus: source addresses, regions and services the identity has not used before.

```lookup
tool: log_stats
filter:
  user: "{{entity.user}}"
group_by: [ip, action]
window: case_last_seen-7d..case_last_seen+1h
limit: 20
run: on_attach
```

Actions come from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record that field, no actions are listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing happened.

### Were new keys, roles or policies created? {#new-credentials kind=check evidence=note}
Escalate if: new access keys, roles, policies, consents or federation settings appeared.
Benign if: a recorded change by an approved automation or administrator.

### Compromised, suspicious or benign? {#decide kind=decision}
Escalate if: an unexpected session changed privileges or credentials, granted consent, or reached sensitive resources.
Benign if: an unusual location or reputation alone, with no change and an expected owner.
Options:
- compromised: Compromised
- suspicious: Suspicious, not confirmed
- benign: Benign | skips: rotate-key, remove-attacker-resources, workloads-updated

Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.

## Contain

### Disable or rotate the key and revoke sessions {#rotate-key kind=action d3fend=D3-CR}

Disable or rotate the key, revoke the identity's sessions and tokens, and record the change reference.

## Eradicate

### Remove attacker-created keys, roles and resources {#remove-attacker-resources kind=action}

Remove every key, role, policy, consent and resource the attacker created, after you have recorded them.

## Recover

### Are workloads using the new credentials? {#workloads-updated kind=check evidence=note}
Escalate if: the old key is still in use, or new unexpected activity appears.
Benign if: every workload runs on the new credentials and the old ones are gone.

### Record the outcome and what you would change {#record-outcome kind=record}

Write how the identity was exposed and what would have limited it, such as shorter-lived keys or tighter permissions.

definition.title: Compromised account or suspicious sign-in
definition.summary: A sign-in that does not fit the account, such as impossible travel or a new device. Confirm with the user, then take the account back if needed.
definition.use_when: A detection reports impossible travel, a risky or unfamiliar sign-in, or other signs that someone else is using an account.
definition.prerequisites: Identity provider sign-in logs; a trusted way to reach the user; access to revoke sessions and reset passwords.

steps.title: Sign-ins for this account in the last 7 days
steps.instructions: The outcome comes from the ECS field `event.outcome`. A source that names it differently shows the sign-ins without their outcome.
steps.focus: new source addresses, countries or devices compared with the user's usual ones.

steps.title: Does the user confirm the sign-in?
steps.focus: ask the user through a channel you trust, not by replying to the alert.
steps.escalate_if: the user did not sign in, or cannot be reached and the sign-in is unusual.
steps.benign_if: the user confirms travel, a VPN or a new device that explains it.

steps.title: Reputation of the sign-in IP
steps.focus: hosting providers, anonymising services and known hostile addresses.

steps.title: Were MFA settings, mail rules or app consents changed?
steps.escalate_if: new MFA methods, mail forwarding rules or app consents appeared after the sign-in.
steps.benign_if: nothing changed after the sign-in, or the user made the changes on purpose.

steps.title: Compromised, suspicious or benign?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: the user denies the sign-in, or the account was changed after it.
steps.benign_if: the user confirms the sign-in and nothing changed.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and reset the password
steps.instructions: End every session and refresh token, then reset the password with the user.

steps.title: Remove attacker-added MFA methods, rules or consents
steps.instructions: Remove every MFA method, mail rule and app consent the user did not add.

steps.title: Is the account back under the owner's control?
steps.escalate_if: new sign-ins from the attacker's addresses appear after the reset.
steps.benign_if: only the owner signs in, from usual places, with their own MFA.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write how the account was taken over, if it was, and what would have stopped it.

definition.title: Data exfiltration
definition.summary: Data may be leaving the network without permission. Measure what moved and where, decide whether it was allowed, and stop it if not.
definition.use_when: A detection reports unusual data collection, staging, bulk downloads, DNS tunnelling or transfers to an external destination.
definition.prerequisites: Proxy, firewall, DNS or cloud storage logs; someone who knows the data and its owner.

steps.title: Volume and destinations of the transfer
steps.instructions: Destinations come from the ECS field `destination.ip` and actions from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record one of them, it is not listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing moved.
steps.focus: destinations, volume and timing compared with the account's normal use.

steps.title: Is the destination a sanctioned service?
steps.focus: the destination against the list of approved services, partners and company cloud accounts.
steps.escalate_if: a personal mailbox, an unknown host, a new cloud account or a DNS tunnel.
steps.benign_if: an approved backup, sync or partner service that the data owner uses.

steps.title: Reputation of the destination
steps.focus: newly registered, hosting or file-sharing destinations and known hostile ones.

steps.title: What data was involved and who owns it?
steps.focus: the repository, file names and classification of the data that moved.
steps.escalate_if: customer, financial, health or credential data, or data under a legal hold.
steps.benign_if: public or test data, or data the account is allowed to move there.

steps.title: Exfiltration, suspicious or benign?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: sensitive data reached an unapproved external destination, or access and transfer records show an unauthorised loss.
steps.benign_if: volume alone, with an approved destination and an authorised user.

steps.title: Block the destination and stop the transfer
steps.instructions: Block the destination at the proxy or firewall and stop the session or job that moves the data.

steps.title: Notify the data owner
steps.instructions: Tell the data owner what moved, when and where, and agree the next steps.

steps.title: Record whether notification duties apply
steps.instructions: Record whether contracts or regulations require you to notify anyone, who decided, and when.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write what left, how, and what would have stopped it, such as a data loss rule or tighter access.

definition.title: Generic incident (NIST 800-61)
definition.summary: A general response procedure for a case no other runbook covers, following the NIST incident response life cycle.
definition.use_when: No other runbook matches the case. Replace it with a specific runbook when you see the same kind of case again.

steps.title: What happened, where, and how bad is it?
steps.focus: the detection, the affected hosts, accounts and data, and the business impact.
steps.escalate_if: production systems, sensitive data or a privileged account is involved, or the activity continues.
steps.benign_if: a known test, a misconfiguration or expected behaviour explains it.

steps.title: Name an incident lead
steps.instructions: Name the person who leads the response until the case is closed.

steps.title: Other alerts for the case's entities in 24 hours
steps.focus: other rules that fired for the same address around the case.

steps.title: What is the scope: which hosts, accounts and data?
steps.escalate_if: more than one host or account, or data leaving the network.
steps.benign_if: one host or account, contained, with no data at risk.

steps.title: Incident, suspicious or benign?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: confirmed malicious activity, or impact on production systems or data.
steps.benign_if: a test, a misconfiguration or expected behaviour.

steps.title: Contain the affected systems or accounts
steps.instructions: Isolate hosts, disable accounts or block addresses as the scope needs. Record each change.

steps.title: Remove the cause
steps.instructions: Remove the malware, access or misconfiguration that caused the incident.

steps.title: Restore normal service
steps.instructions: Bring systems back into service and watch them closely for a while.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write what happened and what you would change. If this kind of case comes back, write a specific runbook for it.

Benign if: one host or account, contained, with no data at risk.

### Incident, suspicious or benign? {#decide kind=decision}
Escalate if: confirmed malicious activity, or impact on production systems or data.
Benign if: a test, a misconfiguration or expected behaviour.
Options:
- incident: Incident
- suspicious: Suspicious, not confirmed
- benign: Benign | skips: contain-systems, remove-cause, restore-service

Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.

## Contain

### Contain the affected systems or accounts {#contain-systems kind=action}

Isolate hosts, disable accounts or block addresses as the scope needs. Record each change.

## Eradicate

### Remove the cause {#remove-cause kind=action}

Remove the malware, access or misconfiguration that caused the incident.

## Recover

### Restore normal service {#restore-service kind=action}

Bring systems back into service and watch them closely for a while.

## Close and learn

### Record the outcome and what you would change {#record-outcome kind=record}

Write what happened and what you would change. If this kind of case comes back, write a specific runbook for it.

definition.title: Phishing or reported suspicious email
definition.summary: A suspicious message reached our mailboxes, or a user reported one. Find every copy, judge the lure and act on anyone who clicked.
definition.use_when: A mail detection fires, or a user reports a message as phishing, spam or a scam.
definition.prerequisites: Mail gateway and mail server logs; proxy or endpoint logs to see clicks; access to remove messages from mailboxes.

steps.title: Find the message and every copy in the mail logs
steps.instructions:
Use the recipients and actions to see how far the message reached and whether the gateway delivered, rejected or quarantined it.

Actions come from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record that field, no actions are listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing happened.
steps.focus: recipients and delivery actions for the sending address around the case window.

steps.title: Is the sender or domain impersonating us or a partner?
steps.instructions: Compare the sender domain with our own domains and those of our partners, letter by letter.
steps.focus: sender address, display name, reply-to address and look-alike domains.
steps.escalate_if: the sender imitates our domain, an executive or a partner, or the reply-to differs from the sender.
steps.benign_if: a known newsletter or marketing sender that a user reported by mistake.

steps.title: Reputation of the sender domain, links and attachments
steps.focus: the sender domain's reputation; check each link and attachment hash the same way.

steps.title: Did anyone click a link or open the attachment?
steps.instructions:
Look in proxy and endpoint logs for each recipient, not only the one named on the case.

Actions come from the ECS field `event.action` and domains from the ECS field `url.domain`. If the source does not record one of them, it is not listed; that means the field is missing, not that nobody clicked.
steps.focus: web requests and file opens by the recipients after the message arrived.

steps.title: Did anyone enter credentials?
steps.focus: sign-ins for the recipients from new places or devices after the message arrived.
steps.escalate_if: a recipient opened the link and then signed in from a new address or device.
steps.benign_if: nobody opened the link, or the page did not ask for credentials.

steps.title: Malicious, suspicious or benign?
steps.instructions: Record what you based the decision on. Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: the message carried a lure that reached real mailboxes, or anyone clicked or entered credentials.
steps.benign_if: a legitimate message that a user reported by mistake.

steps.title: Remove the message from every mailbox
steps.instructions: Quarantine or delete every copy, including those in junk folders. Record how many messages you removed.

steps.title: Block the sender and links at the mail and web gateways
steps.instructions: Block the sending address or domain and every malicious link. Record the change reference.

steps.title: Reset credentials of anyone who entered them
steps.instructions: Reset the password, end the user's sessions and check that MFA is still the user's own.

steps.title: Tell affected users what happened and what to watch for
steps.instructions: Tell the recipients what the message was, what to do if they clicked, and how to report the next one.

steps.title: Tell the reporter what you found
steps.instructions: Thank the person who reported it and tell them the outcome in plain words.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write what happened, what you did, and what would have caught it sooner, such as a gateway rule or user training.

definition.title: Privileged access misuse and insider activity
definition.summary: A privileged account did something outside its approved work. Check whether a change covers it and whether it fits the person's role.
definition.use_when: A detection reports privileged or administrative access that no change explains, or unusual activity by an insider.

steps.title: Is the activity covered by an approved change or ticket?
steps.focus: the change calendar, open tickets and on-call duty for this account and time.
steps.escalate_if: no change, ticket or on-call duty covers the activity.
steps.benign_if: an approved change or an on-call task covers it.

steps.title: Privileged actions by this account in 7 days
steps.instructions: Actions come from the ECS field `event.action`. If the source does not record that field, no actions are listed; that means the field is missing, not that nothing happened.
steps.focus: administrative actions, their targets and their times.

steps.title: Does the activity match the person's role?
steps.instructions: Keep what you learn about the person to the people who need it.
steps.focus: what the person's role needs, compared with what the account did.
steps.escalate_if: access to data or systems outside the role, at unusual hours or in unusual volume.
steps.benign_if: normal duties for the role at expected times.

steps.title: Involve HR or legal as your policy requires
steps.instructions: Record who you involved, when, and what they asked you to do.

steps.title: Misuse, suspicious or authorised?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.

steps.benign_if: authorised access from an expected place by the account owner.

steps.title: Remove or reduce the account's privileges
steps.instructions: Remove the privileges the account does not need, or lock it while the review continues.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write what happened and whether access reviews or approvals should change.

definition.title: Ransomware or destructive activity
definition.summary: Files are being encrypted or destroyed. Stop the spread first, then remove the attacker and restore from backup.
definition.use_when: A detection reports mass file encryption, ransom notes, deleted shadow copies or other destructive changes.
definition.prerequisites: Endpoint and file server telemetry; access to isolate hosts and disable accounts; a tested backup.

steps.title: Are files being encrypted or deleted right now?
steps.instructions: Treat this as urgent until you know the answer. Do not reboot affected hosts; it can destroy evidence.
steps.focus: the file change rate, ransom notes, deleted shadow copies and the process making the changes.
steps.escalate_if: encryption or deletion is still running, or more than one host or share is affected.
steps.benign_if: a known backup, archive or compression job explains the file changes.

steps.title: Declare an incident and name an incident lead
steps.instructions: Declare an incident under your response plan and name the person who leads it.

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts and shares
steps.instructions: Isolate every affected host and take affected shares offline. Record what you isolated.

steps.title: Disable accounts used by the attacker
steps.instructions: Disable or lock the accounts that started the encryption, including service accounts.

steps.title: Which hosts show the same activity?
steps.focus: other cases from the same detection rule, and the hosts they name.

steps.title: Remove the attacker's tools and access
steps.instructions: Remove the attacker's tools, persistence and remote access, and reset credentials they may have.

steps.title: Are backups intact and unaffected?
steps.escalate_if: backups were deleted, encrypted or are reachable with the attacker's credentials.
steps.benign_if: offline or immutable backups are intact and a test restore works.

steps.title: Restore data from backup
steps.instructions: Restore systems and data from clean backups, oldest affected systems last.

steps.title: Are restored systems working and monitored?
steps.escalate_if: encryption starts again, or the attacker's tools reappear.
steps.benign_if: restored systems work normally under close monitoring.

steps.title: Notify legal, leadership and any regulator as required
steps.instructions: Record who you notified, when, and under which duty.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write the timeline, the way in, what stopped the spread and what you would change.

definition.title: Scanning and reconnaissance
definition.summary: A source is probing our hosts, ports or web paths. Most scanning is approved or harmless noise; find the exceptions.
definition.use_when: A detection reports port scans, vulnerability scanners or automated probing of web paths.
definition.prerequisites: Firewall, IDS or web server logs; the list of approved scanners and assessments.

steps.title: Is the scanner one of ours or an approved third party?
steps.focus: the source against the scanner inventory, the change calendar and assessment windows.
steps.escalate_if: the source is on no allow list and no assessment covers it.
steps.benign_if: an approved scanner or assessment covers this source and this time.

steps.title: How many hosts and ports were touched?
steps.instructions: Targets come from the ECS fields `destination.ip` and `destination.port`. A source that names them differently shows the count without the targets.
steps.focus: breadth across many hosts versus depth on one service.

steps.title: Has this source scanned us before?
steps.focus: earlier cases from the same source and how they ended.

steps.title: Approved, repeated hostile scanning, or one-off noise?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: the scanner achieved execution, created a file or process, or no approved assessment covers it.
steps.benign_if: an approved assessment, or one-off internet noise with no successful request.

steps.title: Block the source if scanning repeats
steps.instructions: Block the source at the edge if it keeps scanning. Record where you blocked it.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write what was scanned and whether the scanner list or a detection threshold should change.

  rule_ids: [suricata, et_scan, nessus-openvas, nessus, openvas, nikto, automated_vulnerability_scanning, suspicious_web_shell_execution]
retrieval_queries:
  - web scanner triage
  - approved vulnerability assessment
  - network reconnaissance detection
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1595/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/
  - https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final
---

## Triage

### Is the scanner one of ours or an approved third party? {#approved-scanner kind=check evidence=note}
Focus: the source against the scanner inventory, the change calendar and assessment windows.
Escalate if: the source is on no allow list and no assessment covers it.
Benign if: an approved scanner or assessment covers this source and this time.

### How many hosts and ports were touched? {#hosts-ports kind=lookup}
Focus: breadth across many hosts versus depth on one service.

```lookup
tool: log_stats
filter:
  ip: "{{entity.ip}}"
group_by: [destination.ip, destination.port]
window: case_first_seen-1h..case_last_seen+1h
limit: 20
run: on_attach
```

Targets come from the ECS fields `destination.ip` and `destination.port`. A source that names them differently shows the count without the targets.

### Has this source scanned us before? {#previous-scans kind=lookup}
Focus: earlier cases from the same source and how they ended.

```lookup
tool: related_cases
filter:
  entity: "{{entity.ip}}"
window: case_last_seen-30d..case_last_seen
limit: 10
run: on_attach
```

### Approved, repeated hostile scanning, or one-off noise? {#decide kind=decision}
Escalate if: the scanner achieved execution, created a file or process, or no approved assessment covers it.
Benign if: an approved assessment, or one-off internet noise with no successful request.
Options:
- approved: Approved scanning | skips: block-source
- hostile: Repeated hostile scanning
- noise: One-off noise | skips: block-source

Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.

## Close and learn

### Block the source if scanning repeats {#block-source kind=action optional react=RA3101}

Block the source at the edge if it keeps scanning. Record where you blocked it.

### Record the outcome and what you would change {#record-outcome kind=record}

Write what was scanned and whether the scanner list or a detection threshold should change.

definition.title: Web application attack
definition.summary: A request against one of our web applications looks like an attack. Find out whether any request succeeded and whether the component is exposed.
definition.use_when: A WAF, web server or application detection reports injection, path traversal, session abuse, a dangerous upload or a web shell.
definition.prerequisites: WAF and web server logs with status codes and response sizes; the owner of the application.

steps.title: Requests from this source to the application
steps.instructions: Paths and status codes come from the ECS fields `url.path` and `http.response.status_code`. A source that names them differently shows the count without them.
steps.focus: which paths the source requested and which status codes it got back.

steps.title: Did any request succeed (2xx or unusual size)?
steps.focus: status codes, response sizes and paths that differ from the blocked requests.
steps.escalate_if: an attack request returned 2xx with an unusual size, or a file was written or run on the server.
steps.benign_if: every request was blocked or returned an error, with normal response sizes.

steps.title: Reputation of the source
steps.focus: known scanners, hosting providers and hostile addresses.

steps.title: Is the targeted component vulnerable to this attack?
steps.focus: the application, version and patch level behind the targeted path.
steps.escalate_if: the component is unpatched for the technique, or the request reached an admin or upload endpoint.
steps.benign_if: the component is not affected, or a WAF rule blocks the technique.

steps.title: Exploited, attempted or benign?
steps.instructions: Recording a decision does not change the verdict or close the case.
steps.escalate_if: confirmed account misuse, destructive administration, an executable upload or lasting impact on the service.
steps.benign_if: automation or scanning with no successful request and no impact.

steps.title: Block the source or request a WAF rule
steps.instructions: Block the source, or ask for a WAF rule against the technique. Record the change reference.

steps.title: Patch or take the component offline when exploited
steps.instructions: Patch the component, or take it offline with the application owner until it is fixed.

steps.title: Record the outcome and what you would change
steps.instructions: Write what was attempted, what worked, and what would have stopped it earlier.
